independence.method: Independently check the proposed finite-dimensional mathematical implications and compare source-facing claims against the pinned primary HTML. Constructor names in the packet are implementation obligations, not independently inspected declarations.

scope.general_provider: Every n : Nat, including n = 0, and real symmetric positive definite precision A; actual centered Gaussian covariance A inverse equals Euclidean volume.withDensity of ofReal(sqrt(det A)/(2*pi)^((n:Real)/2) * exp(-coord(x) dot (A*coord(x))/2)).
scope.source_adapter: n >= 3, kappa >= 4, arbitrary O in full O(n), with the literal Eq. (4) precision; source symmetry and Eq. (26) produce positive definiteness internally before invoking the same general provider.
scope.not_certified: No compilation, actual declaration expansion, proof-body dependency, theorem placement, second-consumer completion, or downstream mixture, TV, Poisson, amplification, or main lower-bound claim.

source_checks.finding: The source fixes kappa >= 4 and 3 <= n <= d and defines A_O for every O in O(n). The local single-block density identity has no dependency on ambient d, so omitting d and n <= d from this adapter is a harmless local abstraction. The coefficient of O + transpose O is exactly -(kappa-1)/4.

The source uses N(0,A_O inverse) as the component law and explicitly calls p_O its density. Thus the proposed identity makes standard Gaussian background explicit; it does not replace or correct the source law. Haar distribution in the surrounding integration argument does not restrict a pointwise identity for arbitrary O.

Orthogonality gives norm(Ov)=norm(v), and Cauchy-Schwarz gives absolute inner(v,Ov) <= norm(v)^2. The exact source quadratic form yields norm(v)^2 <= v transpose A_O v <= kappa*norm(v)^2; symmetry is explicit. For nonzero v the lower bound is strictly positive. This proves source precision SPD for every determinant sign, with no caller SPD premise.

The source uses the standard precision-density real normalizer and quadratic exponent. These locations corroborate the density convention only; the surrounding integral, cancellation, separation, and TV steps are not reviewed.

nodes.basis: Source standing assumptions. Full O(n) retained; no orientation, parity or Haar-typical restriction is needed for this pointwise identity.
Literal Eq. (4), including the exact two coefficients.
Source Eq. (26) and its explicit quadratic-form proof; kappa >= 4 implies the coefficient kappa-1 is nonnegative.
The source identifies p_O as the density of the genuine centered Gaussian with inverse-precision covariance.
Standard Euclidean coordinate and Lebesgue-volume identification, including norm-square and quadratic-form coordinate formulas. Euclidean norm is essential; see coordinate caveat.
Source symmetry plus v transpose A v >= norm(v)^2 > 0 for v != 0 gives exactly SPD internally.
SPD is a legitimate hypothesis on a reusable all-finite-dimensional background theorem; dimension zero is admissible.
Finite real SPD matrices have positive determinant and are invertible. Empty determinant is 1; the empty matrix is invertible on the zero space.
The genuine inverse is SPD, has inverse A and determinant 1/det A. Invertibility removes any total-inverse singular fallback.
Positive spectral/CFC square root of the SPD covariance is symmetric SPD, squares to C, and is invertible. Symmetry gives inverse-transpose times inverse equal to C inverse = A.

Correct standard finite-dimensional Gaussian construction by independent scalar standard Gaussians and orthonormal coordinates. The packet requires the existing constructor; actual library declaration identity remains an implementation obligation.
Multiplying scalar Gaussian densities gives (2*pi)^(-n/2) times exp(-sum squares/2); the canonical coordinate volume identification gives the stated actual standard-Gaussian measure identity.

The pushforward by the positive covariance square root is the centered Gaussian with covariance C. Zero translation disappears. The asserted existing-constructor expansion is required, not independently implementation-verified here.
Invertible S represents a continuous linear equivalence on the finite Euclidean space. Its linear determinant is the coordinate matrix determinant, and its inverse is represented by matrix inverse S.
The exact pushforward density is f(L inverse x)/abs(det S); invertibility provides a continuous measurable inverse and the actual Euclidean-volume Jacobian.
Squared inverse-image norm is x transpose (S inverse) transpose (S inverse) x = x transpose A x. No x != 0 assumption is needed.
det S > 0, (det S)^2 = det C = 1/det A imply 1/abs(det S) = sqrt(det A). This concerns S, not the determinant sign of O.

The positive real base 2*pi permits exact real exponent inversion; determinant, exponential and quotient factors are finite and nonnegative. Products of ofReal factors combine into one ofReal. The resulting density is continuous and measurable.
Expand the canonical Gaussian through B6, replace the standard measure using B5, and apply B8 to obtain the genuine transformed density identity.
The zero-dimensional Euclidean space is a singleton. Empty product, determinant and Jacobian are 1, quadratic is 0, real exponent is 0, and its volume and Gaussian are both unit point mass.

Pointwise quadratic, determinant and real-normalizer simplification in T0 gives the exact all-SPD precision density, including the zero-dimensional case; this is standard background rather than a new paper theorem.
The same G1 specializes to the literal source precision using SSPD internally. No source-facing density, inverse, Jacobian, normalization, covariance or SPD premise is introduced.
The original standard Gaussian is a probability measure and measurable pushforward preserves its mass. The displayed density integrates to 1 as a consequence of equality of measures.
A plausible future reuse boundary: a fixed-spectrum precision needs its own SPD proof before G1. This node asserts a plan only and proves no second consumer or reduction.

nonblocking_precision_notes.note: Interpret R^n here with its Euclidean norm. In Lean the bare Pi type Fin n -> Real normally carries a sup norm, so WithLp.ofLp into that default normed type is not an isometry for n > 1. The needed valid statements are the Euclidean norm-square coordinate formula and measure-preserving coordinate identification with product Lebesgue volume. Any implementation should not assert a false isometry into the default Pi norm. This does not invalidate the intended mathematical topology.

Acceptance specifies which actual existing measures and shared-provider call must be checked. The permitted two source files cannot independently certify library constructor definitions, declaration existence, compilation, or the actual implementation dependency from T1 to G1. These are deliberately unverified implementation obligations, not mathematical/source blockers.
